findings.title: F-61 addressed: requireActiveProcess() now selects the deployed process by name
findings.detail: The query adds AND Name IN :STANDARD_PROCESS_NAMES and drops LIMIT 1. The old if (processes.isEmpty()) / Assert.isTrue(false, ...) pair is replaced with Assert.areEqual(1, processes.size(), ...), which fails loudly both when the named process is missing/inactive and when more than one row matches -- a duplicate-match case LIMIT 1 could never surface because it silently kept only the first row.

findings.title: Process name choice: Standard, not Premier, grounded in D-M1S01-04
findings.detail: artefacts/M4-S02/entitlementProcesses/ ships both First_Response_Premier and First_Response_Standard. decisions.md D-M1S01-04 records that Account.Support_Tier__c carries no field default because the contracted tier is a contractual fact about the account; this test's Account fixture is synthetic and has no such fact behind it, so asserting Premier (the higher, opt-in tier) would be the same category of error D-M1S01-04 already rejected for the field itself. Standard is the only choice that does not silently assert a fact the fixture does not have.

evidence.note: D-M1S01-04: also rejected -- defaulting Support_Tier__c to Standard; the contracted tier is a contractual fact about the account; a default would silently assert one

findings.recommendation: None -- recorded as the grounding for a choice the task required, not a defect.

findings.title: SlaProcess.Name spelling is UNVERIFIED; both candidates queried rather than guessed
findings.detail: artefacts/M4-S02/deploy-order.md section 4.1 establishes that this build's <name> metadata attribute is First_Response_Standard (matching the declared file base name) and that only the separate, derived SlaProcess.NameNorm field is documented as being lower-cased by the platform. Neither skills/apex/entitlement-apex-hooks nor skills/admin/entitlements-and-milestones states whether the Name field itself preserves the underscore form or displays a space-separated label. The fix queries both spellings via an IN clause and asserts exactly one match, which settles the question empirically at run 7 without the test needing to guess it now.

findings.recommendation: Once run 7 shows which spelling matched, a follow-up could narrow STANDARD_PROCESS_NAMES to the confirmed one -- not required, since the IN-clause form is stable either way.
